root_motivation: The launch plan runs three traffic waves three days apart and needs to know which one produced each tenant, but `signup(attribution, source_ip, ...)` (src/control.rs) only ever recorded provenance CLASS (synthetic/external) and computed origin -- every external stranger looked identical, with no caller-claimed channel label. Separately, the only abuse brake on signups was the per-IP rate limit read once at startup (MCPHOST_SIGNUP_RATE_LIMIT_PER_HOUR); there was no way to stop a bad-hour abuse spike short of a redeploy through mcphost-deploy, which the operator explicitly wants to avoid doing at 2am on launch night (PRD Problem statement, citing Railway/Fly both losing their free tiers to exactly this kind of unbraked abuse). This PRD gives `signup` an optional, caller-claimed `source` string (stored, echoed, broken out in admin healthz) and a file-based pause kill switch an operator can flip with one `touch`/`rm` over ssh, in under a second, with no restart and no redeploy.
user_persona: Three (PRD User stories): (1) Operator: posts the HN link with `source: "hn"` and the Reddit link with `source: "reddit"` in each snippet; the next morning healthz tells them signups per source. (2) Operator: mining bots start signing up at 3am; they `touch` the pause file over ssh and signups stop while existing tenants keep running unaffected. (3) Agent: calls signup during a pause and gets a clear, structured `signup_paused` error naming when to retry, never a 500 or an opaque failure.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given signup(name, source: "hn"), When it succeeds, Then the response echoes source: "hn" and the tenant row has signup_source = 'hn'.
Given signup(name) with no source, When it succeeds, Then signup_source is NULL and the response omits or nulls source.
Given source: "HN!" or a 65-character value, When signup is called, Then invalid_argument (this crate's args_invalid code) names source and no tenant is created.

Given the pause file is created while the server runs, When signup is called 1s later, Then the error code is signup_paused, message equals the file's first line, and retry_after_secs is present; When the file is removed, Then a signup 1s later succeeds. No restart in between.
Given the pause file exists, When an existing tenant calls host.tool_call, host.trigger.fire, and billing.status, Then all succeed as before.
Given three external signups with sources hn, hn, reddit and one synthetic signup, When admin healthz is read, Then signups_by_source.external is {"hn": 2, "reddit": 1} and signups_enabled is true.
Given the pause file exists, When admin healthz is read, Then signups_enabled is false and signup_pause_message matches the file.

Given 50 concurrent signups while the pause file is toggled on mid-burst, When the burst completes, Then every response is either success or signup_paused, never a 500, and tenant count equals the success count.
Given www/llms.txt on the built tree, When grepped, Then it documents source and lists hn and registry.
Given a pause file whose second line is until=<now+120>, When signup is called, Then retry_after_secs is between 100 and 120.

scope: migrations/0032_signup_source.sql (new): tenants.signup_source TEXT NULL (additive ALTER TABLE) plus an index -- the one migration this PRD's own Migration/compatibility section calls for.

src/state.rs: is_valid_signup_source (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$, 1-64 chars, same hand-rolled-byte-check shape as the pre-existing is_valid_synthetic_label -- this crate has no regex dependency); the new SignupPause type (from_env(data_dir), path(), status() -- a fresh fs::read_to_string per call, never cached) plus SignupPauseStatus and the SIGNUP_PAUSE_DEFAULT_MESSAGE/SIGNUP_PAUSE_DEFAULT_RETRY_AFTER_SECS constants; AppState gains a signup_pause: SignupPause field.

src/errors.rs: AppError::signup_paused(message, retry_after_secs) (a Structured variant, code "signup_paused", data.retry_after_secs) plus its jsonrpc_code mapping alongside the existing rate_limited (both are caller-state "come back later" gates, INVALID_REQUEST).

src/control.rs: signup() checks state.signup_pause.status() first, before the disk-floor guard, before any write, returning signup_paused when Some; validate_source(args) parses/validates the optional source argument (InvalidArgs on a non-string or a value failing is_valid_signup_source, code args_invalid, field source) before the rate-limit admit so a rejected source never consumes a rate-limit slot or creates a row; the validated source flows into Db::create_tenant_attributed_with_source and is echoed back into both the raw-key and handoff-mode response bodies (present only when Some, per AC2's "omits ... when absent").

src/http.rs: /healthz (admin-authenticated body) gains signups_by_source / signups_by_source_24h (each {"external": {source: count}}, additive, always present) and signups_enabled (mirrors state.signup_pause.status().is_none(), fresh per request) / signup_pause_message (present only while paused).

additional.source_is_display_only_never_provenance: Technical considerations: "Keep source separate from origin/origin_detail; provenance is computed, source is claimed by the caller and therefore untrusted (display only)" -- signup_source never feeds classify_source_class/derive_origin, and signups_by_source's own query filters on the host-computed origin = 'external', not on anything source-derived, so a caller cannot spoof its way into (or out of) the external bucket by choosing a source string.
additional.pause_file_is_never_cached: Requirement 3: "the check is per request (stat), never cached beyond 1s" -- SignupPause::status() does a fresh std::fs::read_to_string on every call with no interior-mutability cache layer at all (simpler than a 1s TTL cache and trivially satisfies the 1s upper bound), so an operator's touch/rm takes effect on the very next signup with no restart, exactly AC4's own proof.
additional.signups_by_source_reuses_tenants_not_a_n: signup_events (the per-attempt rate-limit ledger) already has its own count_signup_events_by_origin reader for the pre-existing signups.{external,synthetic} healthz field; this PRD's signups_by_source instead groups the tenants table directly (WHERE origin = 'external' AND signup_source IS NOT NULL GROUP BY signup_source, optionally created_unix >= since for the 24h variant) since every admitted signup writes exactly one tenants row carrying both origin and (now) signup_source already -- a second signup_source column on signup_events would duplicate data this PRD's migration.md explicitly pins to "one additive migration (signup_source TEXT NULL + index)", singular.
additional.signup_paused_reuses_the_structured_erro: AppError::signup_paused follows the exact same Structured-variant, doc-commented constructor pattern as the pre-existing AppError::disk_floor right above it in errors.rs (a code, a message, a data object merged into the JSON-RPC error's own data) rather than a new enum variant -- message is the file's first line verbatim (no wrapping prose), since AC4 requires message to equal it byte-for-byte, and retry_after_secs rides in data the same way disk_floor's free_bytes/floor_bytes already do.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the operator need a way to stop signups without a redeploy?
five_whys_trace.a: The launch plan runs three traffic waves and the only existing abuse brake is a per-IP rate limit read once at startup (MCPHOST_SIGNUP_RATE_LIMIT_PER_HOUR) -- there is no way to react to a bad-hour abuse spike except a redeploy through mcphost-deploy, which the operator explicitly does not want to do at 2am on launch night (Problem statement), and Railway/Fly both lost their free tiers to exactly this unbraked-abuse shape.

five_whys_trace.q: Why a file flag instead of an env var the operator sets and restarts to pick up?
five_whys_trace.a: Technical considerations: "File flag rather than env so mcphost-deploy's env contract is untouched" -- an env-var toggle would need a redeploy to take effect, defeating the whole point (goal 2: "paused and resumed in under a second by a file touch"), and mcphost-deploy's own env contract is out of this PRD's scope to renegotiate.

five_whys_trace.q: Why must the pause check be a fresh stat every call instead of a periodically-refreshed cache?
five_whys_trace.a: Requirement 3's own wording -- "never cached beyond 1s" -- and the success-metrics table's own target ("Pause-to-first-refusal latency: < 1s") both describe a near-immediate reaction; a fresh stat per call is simpler than a bounded-TTL cache and trivially satisfies the bound with no background refresh task to keep alive.

five_whys_trace.q: Why must source be kept separate from the host's own origin/source_class provenance fields instead of folded into them?
five_whys_trace.a: Technical considerations: "provenance is computed, source is claimed by the caller and therefore untrusted (display only)" -- origin/source_class drive real behavior elsewhere (tenants_real counts, synthetic-panel classification); letting an untrusted caller-chosen string influence that would let anyone mislabel their own provenance by picking a convincing source value.

five_whys_trace.q: Why must the pause never affect an authenticated call, a tool run, a trigger fire, or billing?
five_whys_trace.a: Requirement 4's own wording -- "Paused state never affects authenticated calls, tool runs, triggers, or billing" -- and AC5's own scenario (an existing tenant's host.tool_call/host.trigger.fire/billing.status all succeed while paused) both describe the pause as a front-door-only gate: an operator stopping new signups during an abuse spike must not also stop existing, paying tenants' traffic, which is exactly the blast radius a redeploy (the thing this PRD replaces) would have had.
